title: Sentence Titles: An Album a Day
contentHtml:
My friend Ken and I decided to listen to an album every day this year. Each week is themed. At the end of each week, we rank what we listened to. To be clear, we aren’t ranking every album that fits the theme. We are only ranking what we chose to listen to during the last seven days.

This week’s theme is “sentence titles,” meaning albums whose titles are a complete sentence. To make things a little more interesting, the sentence—or series of sentences—had to be at least five words. Thus, albums like Stop by The Plain White-T’s and Go by The Chemical Brothers were not eligible.

#7 If You’re Reading This It’s Too Late by Drake (2015 - 1 sentence, 7 words)

Drake is the rare pop star that can both rap and sing with facility. In fact, I’d go so far as to argue that Drake came close to inventing the rapper-who-can-sing persona that has become common in the pop landscape today. On If You’re Reading This It’s Too Late, you get both sides of Drake. On “Legend” he is singing about how he’s “a motherfucking legend.” On “Energy,” he is rapping about how he’s “got a lot of enemies” trying to drain him of his energy.

Whether he’s rapping or singing, Drake has a lot to say. If You’re Reading This It’s Too Late’s 17 songs run for over an hour. The problem is that while Drake has a lot to say, he doesn’t say much. In fact, nearly every song on this record rotates between four themes: I’m rich (“10 Bands”), I’m awesome (“Legend”), I’m upset (“Energy”), and I’m horny (“Jungle”). This whole album could have been an email.

#6 We Sing. We Dance. We Steal Things. by Jason Mraz (2008 - 3 sentences, 7 words)

I’m told that when you go purchase a fedora, you are legally obligated to prove that you have listened to Jason Mraz’s We Sing. We Dance. We Steal Things. It may be the quintessential guy-with-an-acoustic-guitar-in-a-fedora album. You’ve got the white-boy rap (i.e., “The Dynamo of Volition”). You’ve got the horn-infused blue-eyed soul (i.e., “Butterfly”). You’ve even got the duets perfect to sing with your girlfriend at the local open mic night (i.e., “Lucky”). This is Ed Sheeran without a loop pedal. It is fedora-core.
